## Background

openwashdata publishes water, sanitation and hygiene data as R data
packages. Each package carries a data dictionary, a website and a
citation, all set up with the [washr](https://openwashdata.github.io/washr/)
package. This report shows what a document about one of those datasets
looks like when it renders with the openwashdata brand.^[The brand
definition lives in openwashdata/brand; this document reads it at
render time.]

The `washr` package exposes ten functions. The first three set up the
package structure:

```r
library(washr)
setup_rawdata()
setup_dictionary()
setup_roxygen()
```

### Data sources

Household survey data were collected in three neighbourhoods of Accra
between March and May 2023. @tbl-summary summarises the sample.

| Neighbourhood | Households | Median monthly cost (GHS) |
|:--------------|-----------:|--------------------------:|
| Madina        |        212 |                      48.5 |
| Nima          |        187 |                      61.0 |
| Teshie        |        164 |                      39.2 |

: Sample size and median monthly water cost by neighbourhood {#tbl-summary}

### Methods

Costs were converted to Ghana cedi at the exchange rate of the survey
month. Missing values were not imputed.

::: {.callout-note}
The data package documents every variable in `data-raw/dictionary.csv`.
Run `?watercostaccra` after installing the package to read it.
:::

## Results

Two out of three households pay a vendor for at least part of their
water. The share is highest in Nima, where piped supply is intermittent.

- Vendor water costs about three times the utility tariff per litre.
- Households with a storage tank pay less per month on average.
- Reported costs vary more within neighbourhoods than between them.

## Recommendations

1. Publish the cleaned survey as an R data package with `washr`.
2. Cite the package DOI in every derived report.
3. Refresh the brand with `quarto use brand openwashdata/brand` when it changes.
